Every question starts the same way. You give the three sides their names.

chapter 2 of 5
The three formulas

Three short formulas connect an angle to two of the sides.

slides.title: The three formulas
slides.prompt: Here are the three formulas. Each one uses an angle and two of the sides. You do not have to work them out, you just have to pick the right one. The short word next to each formula is how people remember it.

visual.content:
SOH\(\sin\theta = \dfrac{\textcolor{#ff822c}{\text{opposite}}}{\textcolor{#ff4670}{\text{hypotenuse}}}\)
CAH\(\cos\theta = \dfrac{\textcolor{#00abfa}{\text{adjacent}}}{\textcolor{#ff4670}{\text{hypotenuse}}}\)
TOA\(\tan\theta = \dfrac{\textcolor{#ff822c}{\text{opposite}}}{\textcolor{#00abfa}{\text{adjacent}}}\)

slides.title: Why the sin formula works
slides.prompt: Watch the triangle change size. Every length changes. But opposite divided by hypotenuse stays at $0.50$ the whole time. For a $30°$ angle that answer is always $0.50$, and we call it $\sin 30°$. Drag the corner and try to change it.

slides.title: Why the cos formula works
slides.prompt: Same triangle, different pair of sides. Adjacent divided by hypotenuse stays at $0.87$, whatever size the triangle is. That number is $\cos 30°$.

slides.title: Why the tan formula works
slides.prompt: This pair leaves the hypotenuse out. Opposite divided by adjacent stays at $0.58$, and that number is $\tan 30°$. So every angle has three numbers of its own, and your calculator already knows all of them.

interaction.hint: Name your two sides first. One is opposite $\theta$ and one is the hypotenuse. Then find the formula that uses that pair.

config.successText: The angle of elevation is measured from the flat ground up to your line of sight. The height is opposite it and the ground distance is next to it, so these questions nearly always use tan.
